claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (0007 GMT April 11).
The splashdown marked the safe return of four astronauts from a 10-day lunar mission.
The landing occurred at approximately 20 mph after re-entering the atmosphere at 24,000 mph.
The capsule carried astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The capsule underwent a "skip entry" maneuver to manage heat.
Parachutes deployed to slow the craft to roughly 20 mph for a splashdown.
The crew was retrieved by the USS John P. Murtha using helicopters for extraction.
Artemis II was the first crewed lunar mission since 1972.
The SpaceX Crew-10 and upcoming SpaceX Crew-11 missions to the ISS have utilized similar parachute-assisted splashdowns in the same region, notes this YouTube video.
